title: Signature-hash SLI: compact token-latency signatures and regional failover rehearsal dashboard
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: Current token-level SLI pipelines produce high-cardinality time-series and large traces for every suspect request; this increases storage cost and makes fast clustering/attribution for regional failover noisy. Goal: produce a compact, searchable signature for token-latency patterns (and correlated KV/cache signals) that preserves anomaly-fingerprint quality while reducing ingest/storage by ~8-10x. Use signatures to power a regional rehearsal dashboard that visualizes cohort drift, identifies likely fault domains (model kernel / shard / network / KV miss), and drives automated canary/failover rehearsals.
design_notes: Approach: capture a small vector of quantized token-latency percentiles + kv-hit ratio + emit-time sketch, then run a locality-sensitive hash (LSH) / min-hash variant to produce a 64-bit signature. Signatures are stored as time-series indexes and linked to sampled full traces on demand. Key trade-offs: sampling frequency vs detection sensitivity; signature collision risk vs compression ratio; privacy concerns when signatures could correlate to user prompts (mitigate via prompt token redaction and differential sampling). We will prototype with an eBPF-based timing sidecar for fast per-shard sampling and use a lightweight aggregator to compute signatures before export to TSDB. Backfill/rehash capability required for post-mortem analysis.
implementation_plan: 1) Prototype signature algorithm in Python/Go using production traffic capture (week 1). 2) Implement eBPF sampler + aggregator binary (week 2). 3) Export signatures to dedicated TSDB index and wire dashboard panels (week 3). 4) Integrate with alert rules and rehearsal playbook: scheduled failover rehearsals that replay synthetic traffic mapped to signature clusters (week 4). 5) Iterate sampling rate and LSH parameters based on ROC-style detection curves (week 5).
updates: 2025-02-12: Spike results: min-hash 64-bit signatures on a two-day sample reduced index cardinality by 9x while preserving 92% of high-severity anomaly matches vs full-trace clustering.

2025-02-18: Prototype eBPF sampler (poC) built; initial integration with local aggregator. Observed <1% CPU overhead at 200rps per core. Need tighter tail-percentile quantization to reduce collisions.

2025-02-25: Design review with Observability and SRE. PM requested stronger mapping to customer-visible SLOs — added KV-hit and model-kernel-id fields to signature input. Security flagged prompt-redaction requirement; added redaction step to pipeline.

2025-03-01: Dashboard mock-ups posted (Confluence). GitHub PR opened for signature generator: github.com/redwood-inference/reliability/PR-4987. Initial PR feedback: add deterministic seeding for hash function and a feature-flag to toggle signature export per-tenant.

2025-03-05: Began wiring alerts tied to signature-cluster surge (threshold + growth rate heuristic). Next: run a controlled rehearsal in staging for multi-region failover and tune circuit hysteresis settings.
acceptance_criteria: Compact signatures are produced for >=95% of sampled requests and reduce TSDB index cardinality by >=6x in a production-like workload
Signature clusters map to root cause categories (network, kv-miss, kernel, model) with >=80% precision in post-mortem labeling
Dashboard provides region/cohort view, recent signature growth trend, and an action button to trigger a staged failover rehearsal
Playbook for rehearsals exists in Confluence and documents steps for canary, full failover, and rollback
Feature-flag and tenant opt-out present; prompt content redaction implemented and verified by Security
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Hash collisions leading to false attribution. Mitigation: tune signature dimensionality and collision monitoring; fall back to sampled full traces for suspected clusters.
Risk: Cost of sampling/aggregation at scale. Mitigation: adaptive sampling based on traffic cohort and SLO priority; implement rate-limiter at sidecar.
Risk: Privacy leakage from signatures. Mitigation: redaction + entropy cap + tenant opt-out flag.

Risk: Over-reliance on signatures for automated failover. Mitigation: require multi-signal confirmation (signature surge + golden signal thresholds + synthetic-prober failure) before automated actions.
